touches.text: HYPOTHESIS marks a mechanism written as a first draft so that experiments have something to be wrong about. It is not a decision; what the experiments show replaces it (Law 3). Why? Because evidence always wins.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.

A ticket's plan is a plan, not a list of decisions: constraints, outcomes and resources. - Outcomes, not tasks: each is a claim a proof can check. An outcome hides the how. - Constraints: the bounds, and every how Akien is attached to (encapsulation, the bus as the only channel). - Order comes only from real dependencies (you can't test the bus envelope shape until the bus works), and those also set ticket order. - Resources: existing machines, tools and design patterns, named when they need stating. - A plan too big splits into tickets. Early steps can reshape later ones, so the whole is checked for coherence at the end. -amm
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.
VERBS: run, notices, CodeMother's verbs reached over the bus (RULE 1). COMMANDS: cairn codemother test (--hollow, --seal, --exec, ...), shortcut cairn test; proofgate (the hook: proofs run by hand).

The seal is checked where the proof runs, not in the command's text: a proof refuses to run outside the tester's seal, so no spelling reaches the live ~/.cairn. proofgate only rewrites the common spelling for convenience. CC's decision, Q#101.

Owns the Claude Code hooks: mail check, the turn-shape and ask scans, the gates on record writes and deletes. Anything that adapts CC specifically to Cairn goes in the CC device, and every one of CC's scripts lives here.

A hook registration in .claude/settings.json that a cast ticket's decisions name is approved in advance: it lands at that ticket's BUILDME without a question. WHY: a peer cannot relay Akien's approval of its own hooks, and the ticket is where he already delegated build authority, so the approval names the change, never a messenger. - CC

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
Proofs run against a TESTING database, separate from live.
